claims.description: scripts/ci-concurrency-contract.test.ts reproduces GitHub's one-running/one-pending replacement behavior on a single shared main-ref group: sha-1 running, sha-2 pending, sha-3 displaces sha-2, retained SHAs = ['sha-1','sha-3']. Groups for both the baseline and the current workflow are produced by one shared GitHub-Actions expression evaluator, so the defect is executed rather than asserted in prose.

Groups derived from the parsed .github/workflows/ci.yml give each main push its own ci-main-<sha> group and all three SHAs are retained (['sha-1','sha-2','sha-3']); pull-request heads still share one PR group with cancel-in-progress true so only the newest head survives. The retention assertion is mutation-sensitive: reverting github.sha to github.ref drops sha-2 and fails it.

No deployment authority, permissions, triggers, or merge-gate settings changed — this rework is test-and-evidence only and `git diff origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` is empty. pnpm check:github-workflow-security passed and the full scripts suite passed (74 suites, 1248 tests).

All three cited runs are recorded in red-green.md with URL, head SHA, created time, attempt count, conclusion and job count, verified read-only via gh api on 2026-08-02. Correction: only 30688886377 and 30688890531 are unrecovered zero-job cancellations; 30688912863 currently concludes success with 4 jobs, but its attempts 1 and 2 were themselves zero-job cancellations before a manual third attempt produced CI evidence. The three head SHAs are consecutive main commits merged inside 46 seconds, matching the pending-run eviction the deterministic contract reproduces; the equivalent concurrency proof is the RED under the pre-fix group line and the restored-workflow rerun, both named per assertion in red-green.md. GitHub-hosted rapid-merge racing was not re-executed.
